_howto: Newest first. Add an entry at the top each time you push an update; the website and the in-game 'What's new' both read this file. tag: new | improved | fixed.

items.text: Sign in arcade style with a name and a four-digit PIN, the same way as Typlympics. It works on any device.
Online leaderboards for every track: Best Laps from Time Trial and Best Races from your season races.
Time Trial: four laps in a standard truck against the clock, chasing the ghost of the fastest driver on the board or your own best. Every lap shows how far ahead of or behind the ghost you are.
Race friends live: make a room, share the 4-letter code or link, and race up to 8 people at once. The host picks the track and can fill empty spots with the season's rivals.
The Aussie 8 logo now heads the in-game menu too.

Sound! A growling V8 that revs with your speed and roars on nitro, tyre scrub in the slides, the pack rumbling past, crunching crashes, wall thumps, landings, pickups, the countdown, roos, Stewards sirens and a crowd that cheers, gasps and boos with the race. All made live in the browser.
Sound settings on the menu (effects and music volume), and M mutes during a race.
Fewer crashes: it now takes a harder, more side-on hit to wreck, Grit makes your ute tougher still, and crashes spin you for less time.
Wreck parts on the track slow down whoever drives over them, then break apart. Parts nobody hits blink out after about 25 seconds, so the track no longer fills up.
A badly damaged ute loses a little top speed and weaves slightly. Grab a spanner to straighten it out.
Duke is now the blond champion with the sunglasses.
Every track now has race-day set pieces outside the walls: a race-control tower, gazebos, floodlight towers, Aussie flags, a TV camera crane and roo warning signs.
More trackside clutter: barrier blocks, red, white and black tyre stacks, hay bales, oil drums and cones.
New, bigger nitro (lightning bolt) and repair (spanner) pickups that are easier to spot.

notes.title: A crowd that reacts, and Uluru on every course

items.text: Packed grandstands above every track, with a live crowd in the style of NHL '94. Fans jump up for overtakes and lead changes, lean on the rail for close racing and wrecks, flash cameras at big jumps and kangaroos, boo when the Stewards come out, wave flags on the final lap and go wild when you win.
Reactions ripple out from where the action happened, and the section of crowd nearest the trucks gets on its feet. Every so often a Mexican wave rolls across the stands.
Uluru at sunset is now the backdrop on all eight courses, framed between the two grandstands, with a Channel 8 camera and banner trackside.
On phones the score bar at the top is see-through, so you can see the crowd behind it.
New animated FINAL LAP! and RACE FINISHED! announcements, centred over the track.
New Aussie 8 logo in the website and game headers.
The pause screen text sat off to the left. It's centred now.

notes.title: The art library and Road Rash rivals

items.text: New overhead truck art for all eight drivers, with damage that builds up on the truck over a couple of seconds after each hit. Badly damaged trucks smoke.
Wreck debris: tyres, bumpers, glass and oil fly off in crashes and stay on the track for the rest of the race.
Animated crashes, nitro flames, mud spray, water splashes and drift dust, plus kangaroos and emus that leap clear when clipped.
Rivals remember you. Each driver's opinion of you and their temperament decide whether they give you room, block you or hunt you down.
SHUNT (E or X, or the SHUNT button on phones) bumps the truck beside you. Dirty driving brings out the Stewards' ute and a black flag.
Radio banter from rivals mid-race, and a grid moment before every race: taunt, encourage or ignore the driver beside you.
Channel 8 coverage: live bug, starting grid and final lap graphics, and Barry Doolan on the ticker.
Illustrated story events, location backdrops, character portraits and all six season endings.
The Yowie races #6 as the hardest driver in the field. Beat him in the final round and he takes off the helmet.
Each track has its own skyline and scenery, and every crossover carries the gold ring of Hank's Corner.
On narrow phones in portrait, BRAKE could start a steering drag. Every pedal button now sits fully on the pedal side.
Races go fullscreen on phones, with the controls in the space beside the track so your thumbs don't cover the action.
Drag to steer: put your thumb down anywhere on the left and point where you want the truck to go. Gas is automatic.
Buttons mode for players who prefer it: big ◀ ▶ on the left, and GAS with NITRO right beside it so you can roll your thumb across.
Left-handed option that swaps the steering and pedal sides.
NITRO is bigger and sits right under your thumb. BRAKE moves into the side margin in landscape.
Larger lap, position and nitro readouts on phones, plus vibration on crashes where the phone supports it.
Trucks can now pivot away from a wall while you're on the gas instead of getting pinned.
Aussie 8 has a home page, with these dev notes and a What's new panel in the game.
The season now alternates four regular loops with four figure-8s, finishing on the Outback Showdown figure-8.
The countdown and the garage tell you whether the next track is a loop or a figure-8.
Eight trucks per race. New rivals: Shazza Kelly, Tash Kowalski, Thommo Price and Gazza Reid.
Eight unique tracks, each checked so the only place the two halves meet is the crossover.
Crashes: a hard side-on hit spins both trucks out with sparks, flying paint and screen shake.
Points and prize money now pay all eight places: 10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
The scoreboard shows all eight positions, with yours outlined in gold.
The game is now Aussie 8, with a new arcade title screen.
32-bit pixel art: hand-made truck sprites in 32 directions, dithered red-dirt tracks, tyre walls in green and gold, and Uluru at dusk behind the grandstands.
Kangaroos hop across the track. Clip one and you lose speed; the roo just bounces away.
The story moves to the outback: Coober Pedy, Broken Hill, the Gold Coast, utes, roadhouses and a meat pie sponsor.
Arcade off-road racing with nitro, mud, water, jumps and cash pickups. First released as Backroad Stakes.
RPG garage: driver levels, four stats and truck upgrades.
Good, shady and gamble choices between races, a karma meter and a rival who remembers what you did.
A crew of three with trust meters and perks. Push someone too far and they walk.
Six endings, depending on the title result, your karma, your crew and your rival.
